final_answer: Imagine a small beach town where ice cream sales and shark attacks both rise during the summer. At first glance, someone might think eating ice cream causes shark attacks. But the real reason is the weather: hot days drive more people to buy ice cream and also encourage more swimmers in the ocean. The heat is the hidden factor causing both. This shows that just because two things happen together (correlation), it doesn’t mean one causes the other. A third factor — in this case, the weather — might be the true cause.
